sd_data_master.problem: The generated RTL uses registered outputs with default-zero assignments (lines 171-181) that clear every output each cycle before the state case. The reference design (ref_sd_data_master in support.sv) does NOT use defaults; instead, outputs retain their values across states unless explicitly changed. This causes systematic mismatches for all signals that should persist across state transitions (cmd_set, cmd_arg, sys_adr, tx_cycle, rx_cycle, start_tx_fifo, start_rx_fifo, a_cmp_tx, a_cmp_rx, ack_transfer, CIDAT, we_req, d_read, d_write, re_s_tx, re_s_rx, etc.). Each state must explicitly assign only the signals that change, and all others must retain their previous value.
evidence: Trace shows start_tx_fifo expected=1 actual=0 at time 2370 because default clears it after GET_TX_BD sets it to 1
re_s_tx mismatch at time 2310 (original) because re_s_tx not explicitly cleared in GET_TX_BD for bd_cnt>=2
Multiple signals show one-cycle lag pattern (match_rate_dut_lag1 ~0.98) indicating the reference retains values while DUT clears them
Reference support.sv lines 252-509 show no default assignments; each state case only sets signals that need to change

override.action: Remove default-zero assignments (lines 171-181). Ensure every state explicitly sets all signals that need to change in that state. Let all other signals retain their previous values. Match reference output logic exactly: IDLE clears all control signals; GET_TX_BD/GET_RX_BD set BD read signals and retain others; SEND_CMD clears re_s_tx/re_s_rx/start_rx_fifo and sets d_read/d_write/we_req; RECIVE_CMD clears we_req/d_read/d_write and sets start_rx_fifo; DATA_TRANSFER sets CIDAT=1 and manages transfer completion; STOP/STOP_SEND manage their signals.
